actions.description: Publish one iai_control_msgs/MultiJointVelocityImpedanceCommand with the seven desired joint velocities on /r_arm_vel/command. The receipt confirms only that rosbridge accepted the publication, not motion, arrival or stopping.

inputs.description: Seven desired joint velocities in the controller's joint order
inputs.name: joint_velocities

actions.name: publish_joint_velocity

outputs.description: True when the rosbridge publication was handed to the transport
outputs.name: published

outputs.description: Always false for a topic publication: rosbridge carries no execution confirmation
outputs.name: confirmed

facts.text: The README states that the simulation offers a joint velocity/position-resolved interface, that commands are sent to it, and that no dynamics or physics simulation is included.
The README names /r_arm_vel/command as the topic to publish and says the current robot state is published on /joint_states with type sensor_msgs/JointState.
lwr_sim_vel_controllers.launch loads the controller configuration and starts the pr2_controller_manager spawner with the r_arm_vel controller.
The velocity-controller configuration names r_arm_vel, its iai_robot_mechanism_controllers/MultiJointVelocityImpedanceController type and the seven right_arm_0_joint through right_arm_6_joint joints.
MultiJointVelocityImpedanceController subscribes the relative command topic with queue size 1 and creates a state publisher on the relative state topic.
The controller header includes pr2_controllers_msgs/JointTrajectoryControllerState.h.

When loop_count_ % 10 == 0 and the state publisher trylocks, the update assigns header.stamp from the update time, desired.velocities[j] from command[j], actual.positions[j] from position_, actual.velocities[j] from velocity_ and error.velocities[j] from error[j].

The command callback takes an iai_control_msgs::MultiJointVelocityImpedanceCommand; only when its velocity array length equals the configured joint count does it copy the velocities and set watchdog_time_, otherwise it logs an error.
The iai_control_msgs/MultiJointVelocityImpedanceCommand definition declares velocity as a float32 array in rad/s; stiffness, damping and add_torque are also declared.
The controller constructor initializes watchdog_period to 0.1.
The controller header declares watchdog_time_ as ros::Time and watchdog_period as ros::Duration.
The controller update replaces every desired velocity with zero when the time since watchdog_time_ exceeds watchdog_period.
lwr_loopback_sim_controllers.launch sets /use_sim_time false, requests a 250 Hz joint-state publish rate, starts the loopback_controller_manager node and sets dt 0.004 s, damping 0.0 and mass 0.01.

LoopbackControllerManager's init creates a pr2_controller_manager::ControllerManager, reads dt, damping and mass parameters (defaults 0.01, 0.1 and 0.1) and subscribes the private desired_joints topic, whose callback writes the received joint positions into the joint states.
LoopbackControllerManager::simulateJoints integrates commanded effort, damping, mass and dt into joint velocity and then joint position; a comment says KDL should be used for correct dynamics.
kdl_arm_kinematics advertises the private services get_fk, get_ik, get_ik_solver_info, get_fk_solver_info and get_weighted_ik.
urdf_management's service.lisp registers an alter_urdf service.
lasa_to_iai.py subscribes /KUKA/joint_imp_cmd as a JointStateImpedance and publishes /r_arm_pos_controller/command and /r_arm_vel/command.
lasa_to_iai.py republishes the velocity of every /KUKA/joint_imp_cmd message that carries num_dof velocities as a MultiJointVelocityImpedanceCommand on /r_arm_vel/command.
The arm xacro declares joint 0 as revolute with limit lower -170 * M_PI / 180, upper 170 * M_PI / 180, effort 204 and velocity arm_velocity_scale_factor * 110 * M_PI / 180 (an unsigned magnitude).
lwr_start_config.yaml lists the seven right-arm joint names and their positions under joints/name and joints/position.
lwr_simulation.launch includes lwr_realtime.launch with realtime false, the loopback, velocity and position controller launch files, and starts the lasa_to_iai_parser node.

lwr_sim_pos_controllers.launch starts r_arm_state_separator with ~in_joint_states remapped to /joint_states and ~out_joint_states to /r_arm_pos_controller/joint_states, and r_arm_pos_controller (joint_p_ctrl.py) with ~vel_command_out remapped to /r_arm_vel/command.

JController.control_tick returns without publishing when more than rospy.Duration(0.1) has passed since last_command_time, and otherwise publishes the P-controller velocity clipped to max_speed on ~vel_command_out while that publisher has connections.
lwr_sim_vel_controllers.yaml gives every r_arm_vel joint the gains p 2.5, i 0.0 and d 0.0 under the comment 'for perfect sim: chose p=m/dt with damping=0'.
lwr_realtime.launch defaults realtime to true and then starts joint_state_publisher with source_list /KUKA/joint_states and rate 500.
lwr2_realtime.launch starts joint_state_publisher with source_list /KUKA/joint_states and rate 500 without a realtime condition.
lwr2_simulation.launch includes lwr2_realtime.launch, the loopback, velocity and position controller launch files, and starts the lasa_to_iai_parser node.
The README's simulation quick start runs roslaunch kuka_lwr_bringup lwr2_alone_simulation.launch.
The README's realtime visualization starts lwr2_alone_realtime.launch with the kuka_fri_bridge and says the kuka_fri_bridge will be publishing the /joint_states topic.

determinism.notes: Event-driven contract fake with no physics step or pacing; placeholder joint samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic: it answers the declared /joint_states subscription and /r_arm_vel/state confirmation samples and records /r_arm_vel/command publications; it runs no ROS graph, loopback_controller_manager, PR2 or IAI controller, URDF model or physics step

the fake does not reproduce the loopback integration (dt 0.004 s, damping 0.0, mass 0.01 in lwr_loopback_sim_controllers.launch:19-21) or the requested 250 Hz joint-state publish rate (lwr_loopback_sim_controllers.launch:10); its joint samples are placeholders
the launch starts external pr2_controller_manager, IAI velocity/position controllers and the lasa_to_iai parser; none is started or validated here

the controller's 0.1 s watchdog zeroes the desired velocity after a silent period, but the fake does not model the controller or its watchdog; the watchdog is a timeout on silence, not the acknowledged stop

the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): one publication of seven zero velocities on /r_arm_vel/command, achieved only when /r_arm_vel/state shows desired.velocities (the applied command, desired.velocities[j] = command[j]) within the operator bound and the norm of actual.velocities (actual.velocities[j] = velocity_) within the operator bound, in two consecutive fresh stamped samples inside the confirmation window; ROS 1 discards the first sample of the new subscription; thresholds are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds are fake-scale, so a live deployment sets both in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the fake sets measured joint velocity to the commanded velocity at once (a placeholder, not the loopback); it does not integrate simulateJoints and does not model commanded_effort_ or the watchdog; confirmation on the fake is a contract stand-in
the velocity envelope is operator_required; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only, not a device fact
a live run needs the operator's ROS 1 graph and rosbridge; no ROS process, node or hardware is contacted

lwr_simulation.launch also starts lasa_to_iai_parser, which republishes every /KUKA/joint_imp_cmd velocity array (the README's own test publishes one at 20 Hz) on /r_arm_vel/command, and r_arm_pos_controller, which publishes velocities there while position goals arrive on /r_arm_pos_controller/command; either keeps desired.velocities off zero, so the stop stays unconfirmed and latched; this package has no unpause and cannot clear a command those nodes store

lwr_realtime.launch (realtime defaults to true) and lwr2_realtime.launch start joint_state_publisher, which republishes the real arm's /KUKA/joint_states as /joint_states at 500 Hz: in the README's realtime visualization /joint_states is the real KUKA arm, and lwr2_simulation.launch starts it next to the simulation as a second /joint_states publisher; the sensed source is /r_arm_vel/state, not /joint_states; the SDK cannot prove a ROS graph is simulated; a real controller of this class behind /r_arm_vel/command would act on the same publication (R2, out of scope)

the README's quick start names lwr2_alone_simulation.launch, which is not in the pinned clone; lwr_simulation.launch is the single-arm simulation with the loopback manager as the only /joint_states publisher
the fake echoes a commanded velocity into its joint-state sample until the next command, while the controller zeroes the desired velocity after watchdog_period (0.1) without a new command
no ROS graph, rosbridge connection, simulator execution, hardware run or human review has occurred

operator_required.reason: the clone states an unsigned arm-velocity magnitude for each URDF joint and no signed command envelope for /r_arm_vel/command; the operator supplies the reviewed per-joint velocity bound

safe_state.description: Simulated only: seven zero joint velocities on /r_arm_vel/command are the request, not a stop by itself; the stop is achieved only when /r_arm_vel/state shows every applied desired velocity and the norm of the measured joint velocities inside the operator bounds, in two consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation window. Nothing is claimed after it. A competing publisher leaves the stop unconfirmed and latched, and there is no unpause.
